participantInstructions: The event will be presented to you through your reading of the 21st Century Skills, the Performance Indicators, and the Case Study Situation. You will have up to 30 minutes to review the case study situation, discuss it as a team, and prepare your presentation and notes. Both team members must take part in the presentation and in answering the judge's questions. You will be evaluated on how well you meet each of the performance indicators listed for this event. Turn in all of your notes and materials to the judge at the end of the event.
situation:
You are the Customer Experience Manager and the Marketing Communications Manager at CANINE COVE PET COMPANY, a manufacturer of pet grooming and enrichment products that also operates a small chain of boarding and daycare resorts. The founder and CEO (judge) built the company over eighteen years and has asked the two of you to meet before a larger executive meeting. The founder wants your joint recommendation on a decision that affects the pending sale of the company.

Canine Cove operates four pet resorts offering boarding, daycare, and grooming alongside its manufacturing division, and the company has been profitable for eleven consecutive years. The founder (judge) is close to finalizing a sale of the company to a regional hospitality group and plans to retire once the transaction closes in ten weeks. The resorts compete on personalized guest care and attentive service during high-occupancy holiday weekends, when nearly every boarding suite and grooming slot is booked weeks in advance.

The company's longtime guest relations director has resigned to open an independent pet-sitting and boarding service twenty miles away. Her employment contract includes a one-year non-compete clause covering the resorts' service area, and the buyer's due-diligence team has asked whether Canine Cove intends to enforce it before the sale closes. The director personally built relationships with many long-tenured clients, greeting regulars by name and adjusting holiday packages around cultural observances important to individual families.

Guest-communications data pulled by the marketing communications manager shows that most repeat bookings are logged through the resorts' front-desk staff and loyalty app rather than through the director directly, suggesting enforcement would add legal cost without protecting much revenue. Resort staff disagree: employees who work the floor daily insist their most loyal clients booked specifically because of her personal attention, and several are already asking where she is headed next. Some also point to programs she built, including the resorts' employee wellness offerings, as reason to part on good terms.

The founder (judge) wants a recommendation on whether to enforce the non-compete as written, waive it, or negotiate a narrower version limited in scope or duration, grounded in both the booking data and the concerns resort staff have raised. The founder is also weighing whether pursuing enforcement this close to closing could unsettle resort staff or draw public attention during the season when guest experience matters most to the resorts' reputation and to the value the buyer is paying for.

The founder (judge) will greet you in the founder's office, thank you for making time during a demanding week, ask you to share your recommendation and the reasoning behind it, and listen closely to your ideas before the meeting with the buyer's team. After your presentation and the founder's questions, the founder will thank you again for your analysis and conclude the meeting.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder and CEO of CANINE COVE PET COMPANY. Business background is the same as the situation above. You are preparing to retire once the pending sale of the company closes, and you have asked the Customer Experience Manager and the Marketing Communications Manager to recommend whether to enforce, waive, or narrow the non-compete clause against your departing guest relations director. You want their recommendation to weigh the booking data against the concerns your resort staff have raised, and to protect both the company's reputation and the sale you have worked years to reach.

You will greet the participants, ask them to share their recommendation, and listen to their ideas. Ask the following questions after their presentation:
judgeQuestions: Is offering a narrower, shorter non-compete worth considering instead of enforcing the clause as written?
If we let this go, what should we tell staff who feel differently about her impact on clients?
